# WO-2026-08-13-15 — the sense-check and the ShopperBot notification

**Warwick saw Mum's Cockpit on the Fire tablet and accepted it** — *"first time in a long time with fucking
asdair I am happy and smiling."* Then he asked for four things. Two of them are yours.

**⛔ HE ALSO CORRECTED THE FRAMING, AND IT GOVERNS HOW YOU TREAT THIS ORDER:** *"Its not a scope change! Its
a feature request!"* This is ordinary product work on a product he owns. Preflight it properly, then build.

## THE ROUTE CONTRACT — **v3, 2026-08-13. FINAL.** Frozen, and byte-identical in every lane's order.

> **⚠️ v3 SUPERSEDES v2 IN PLACE, which superseded v1.** v2 fixed the defect that told Mum her list was
> sent when nothing had happened. **v3 fixes the one v2 left behind: v2 could not tell "nothing happened
> at all" apart from "I recorded what you sent, but it will not change today's shop."** Keel established
> both by execution on the live route, and both were his catch, not review's.

```
Cockpit (tailnet)   POST /api/asdair/list
   proxies to →     POST http://127.0.0.1:8710/asdair/list

request  { "household": 1,
           "list_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",        <- the date SHE confirmed. Becomes the shop's date.
           "items":  [ { "id": "<regulars.id_display>", "name": "<the name SHE was shown>", "qty": 1..20 } ],
           "extras": [ "<her exact words>", ... ]      <- omit the key entirely when empty
         }

200      { "ok": true, "shop_ref": "...", "shop_id": <n>,
           "created":      true|false,     <- a NEW shop row was written
           "recorded_new": true|false,     <- THIS submission left a durable ledger row
           "matched_by":   "insert"|"shop_ref"|"telegram_message"|"superseded_terminal_ref" }

4xx/5xx  { "ok": false, "error": "<machine_code>", "message": "<ONE plain sentence>" }
```

**Additional keys MAY appear** (`duplicate`, `source_id`, `items`, `superseded_terminal_ref`). **The UI reads
only the keys named above** and must not break when others are present.

**THE THREE OUTCOMES, AND THE UI MUST RENDER THEM AS THREE — this is the whole point of the contract.**

| `created` | `recorded_new` | What actually happened | What she is told, in substance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `true` | `true` | A shop was created from her list | **"Sent."** The sent state. |
| `false` | `true` | Today's shop already existed. **Her changed list IS durably recorded, but it does NOT alter today's shop.** | **"Today's list has already gone. I've told Warwick what you changed."** |
| `false` | `false` | Today's shop already existed and this submission was **identical** — nothing was written at all | **"Today's list has already gone. Nothing has changed."** |

**⛔ `ok:true` ALONE NEVER LICENSES THE WORD "SENT". Only `created:true` does.** *Why: `receiveList` is
idempotent on `(household_id, shop_ref)` and `shop_ref` derives from the date, so a same-day resubmission
resumes rather than creates. Addendum E criterion 9 names the defect this prevents — "any answer that
changes the display but not the durable record."*

**⛔ ROW 2 IS NOT A CONSOLATION MESSAGE. IT IS A PROMISE THAT MUST BE KEPT.** If the UI says Warwick was
told, **the ShopperBot notification MUST actually fire on `recorded_new:true`** — not only on first
submission. A page that claims he was told when he was not is the same defect one layer up.

**⛔ MUM IS NEVER ASKED A QUESTION.** Warwick, 2026-08-13: *"I will deal with any questions and such through
my existing process."* No disambiguation, no candidate list, no "which did you mean" ever reaches her
screen. Ambiguity and genuinely-new items go through and are answered downstream in Warwick's own flow.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — the sense-check, built on the resolver that already exists.**
New `checkItem.js` + `POST /asdair/check-item`, and its Cockpit proxy. **It MUST call `resolveReading` from
`services/asdair/interpret/resolveByCatalogue.js`.** Do not write a second matcher — Larry measured that one
over all 109 real regulars and it returns the exact right regular 107 times, the wrong product 0 times, and
honest ambiguity twice. **It is read-only: `asdair_ro` suffices and you must not open a write pool for it.**

**AC2 — ⛔ THE CHECK NEVER ASKS MUM A QUESTION. This is the criterion most likely to be got wrong, because
the resolver hands you a `needs_confirmation` carrying a candidate list and the obvious thing to do is show
it.** Warwick: *"I will deal with any questions and such through my existing process."*

- `matched` / `possible_duplicate` → return the matched name so the UI can say *"you've already got that"*.
- `needs_confirmation` / `unmatched_new_item` → **return the status and NOTHING she must decide.** Never
  return alternatives to her surface. Ambiguity is resolved downstream, by Warwick, in his own flow.
- **Prove by execution that no response on this route can carry a candidate list.**

**AC3 — `extras` reach the shop as her exact words.**
The adapter accepts `extras: [string]` and folds them into `rawText`. **Do NOT normalise, title-case,
spell-correct or de-duplicate what she typed** — the pipeline resolves identity downstream and her raw words
are evidence. **An extra is never silently dropped**: if one cannot be carried, the submission fails loudly
rather than succeeding with less than she asked for.

**AC4 — `recorded_new` on the response, per contract v3.**
You established the distinction; now expose it. **`created:false, recorded_new:true` MUST be reachable and
MUST be distinguishable in the body** — Felix's page renders three different sentences off these two booleans
and it is already built.

**AC5 — the ShopperBot notification, and it is INTENDED AUTOMATIC.**
New `notifyShopper.js`, calling the EXISTING `services/asdair/bot/sendShopperMessage.js`. **The real
submission event fires it. Not a script, not a manual step, not Larry remembering.**

- Fires when `created:true` **OR** `recorded_new:true`. **Fires NOT AT ALL when nothing was recorded** —
  Warwick must not be pinged by a no-op.
- The message names **Mum**, the shop reference and the item count, and says plainly whether this created
  today's shop or changed an existing one.
- **⛔ A FAILED NOTIFICATION MUST NEVER FAIL HER SUBMISSION.** Her list is durable the moment `receiveList`
  returns; a Telegram outage must not turn a saved shop into an error on her screen. **But it must not be
  silent either** — log it loudly and reflect it in the response, because failure is never silent.
- **⛔ NEVER MESSAGE MUM. NEVER POLL.** `noPolling.test.js` guards the bot module; do not defeat it.
- **You inject `fetchImpl`. You never read `SHOPPER_BOT_TOKEN`.** Your `credential_scope` excludes it
  deliberately, and the module is hermetic by design precisely so this is possible.

**AC6 — the promise in row 2 of the contract is kept.**
Felix's page tells Mum *"I've told Warwick what you changed"* on `recorded_new:true`. **Prove by execution
that this exact case fires exactly one notification.** A page claiming Warwick was told when he was not is
the same defect as a page claiming a list was sent when it was not — one layer up.

- `node services/cockpit/asdair-list-check.mjs` and `node services/cockpit/provenance-check.mjs` → exit 0.
- `bash scripts/secret-scan.sh --surface <your 12 paths>` → exit code AND coverage. **Exit 2 is NOT SCANNED,
  never a pass.**

- **Mum's UI.** `services/cockpit/public/**` is Felix's. **Do not touch it.**
- **The real Telegram send.** Larry does that at integration. **You never contact `api.telegram.org`.**

- `serverConfig.test.js:116`'s port-18710 fixture · the `sw.js` SHELL trap · Mum-Cockpit authentication.

## Sequencing

1. **READ-BACK AND HOLD.** Outcome, plan, what this order failed to settle, what looks wrong. **AC2 and
   AC5's failure semantics are where I most expect you to push back.** Your last read-back changed the
   contract twice and was worth every minute of it.
2. AC1 → AC2 → AC3 → AC4 → AC5 → AC6.
3. Commit on `build-015/b15-50-sense-check-and-notify` in `C:/Fusion247PKA-notify` and **push**. No PR, no

**Warwick's standing constraints:** AsdAIr never checks out, never pays, never chooses a slot, never touches
